OpenCode Guard List

Put one folder or file per line under a heading. Drag it in from Finder or type a
path starting with / or ~. Delete a line to remove it. Lines starting with # are
ignored. Save, then quit and reopen OpenCode.

By default, OpenCode can read and search any files your macOS account permits,
including folders not listed here. An empty READ ONLY section does not restrict
reading.

ALLOW grants permission to create, change, and delete files. READ ONLY removes
write permission, for example from a subfolder inside an ALLOW folder. DENY
blocks both reading and writing. When entries overlap, DENY always wins;
otherwise the most specific entry wins.

OpenCode's required data, cache, and temporary folders remain writable
automatically. See last-launch.log next to this file for the applied locations.
Build tools with their own folders in your home, such as ~/.cargo or ~/go, need
those folders under ALLOW.

ALLOW - agents may create, change and delete things inside these:

READ ONLY - agents may look but never change or delete:

DENY - agents may not read, search, change or delete these:
# Examples; remove the # to use. Denying these breaks git over SSH and cloud tools inside the guard.
# ~/.ssh
# ~/.aws
# ~/.gnupg
